claim_verdicts.claim_text: Spironolactone can explain the initial onset of elevated potassium.

citations.quote: Spironolactone 12.5 mg PO daily was started by outpatient cardiology on 2026-02-19 and taken daily since; last home dose the morning of 2026-03-01, per patient and pharmacy fill history.
Assessment: new hyperkalemia with acute kidney injury; etiology not yet clear (differential includes reduced renal potassium clearance, ACE inhibitor effect and recent spironolactone use).
Assessment: hyperkalemia, likely secondary to spironolactone.

claim_verdicts.why: Spironolactone was taken daily until the morning of 2026-03-01, before the first elevated potassium on 2026-03-02, so the timeline allows it to explain the onset. The record lists it as a differential and later calls the hyperkalemia likely secondary to it, which supports the hedged 'can explain' wording.
claim_verdicts.uncertainty: The record does not confirm the cause; the 2026-03-02 note called the etiology unclear and the first elevated value (5.7 mmol/L at 05:45) is not among the lines shown here. Cause (2026-02-19) precedes effect (2026-03-01T14:20): temporally possible, but timing alone does not prove causation.
